title: Connection sanity lab notes and deploy backout strategy
summary: Lab-run notes and a pragmatic deploy/backout playbook focused on connection-level sanity (TLS handshakes, controlplane RPC versions, port/proxy compatibility) rather than full runtime binary upgrades. Intended as a pre-upgrade gating checklist and a compact rollback recipe for private (VPC/on-prem) cutovers.
content:
Context:
This note captures experiments run in the private-deploy lab cluster (rack-2 lab VLAN) to validate connection-level compatibility between the new control-plane API (v2) and existing runtime nodes (v1 ABI). The goal: detect non-obvious failures that cause slow degradation (connection spikes, intermittent 503s, TLS renegotiation loops) and codify a minimal backout path focused on networking and API shims. Not a full runtime upgrade runbook; complements existing runtime upgrade playbooks but emphasizes the "first-mile" of traffic handoff and connection semantics.

High-level objectives:
- Validate RPC/version negotiation behavior when control-plane and runtime disagree on features (streaming, header compression, keepalive)
- Ensure sidecar/proxy (istio/ambassador) config tolerates header/size differences without dropping streams
- Measure failure modes that don't immediately trigger health checks (slow request growth, connection resets)
- Create a compact backout checklist (network and control-plane focused) that can be executed without rolling runtime binaries

Lab topology used:
- Control-plane: cp-lab-v2 (canary image) behind a small HA pair (2 instances)
- Runtimes: rt-lab-v1 (3 nodes) using local KV cache
- Ingress: envoy sidecars + a simple IPtables nat path for direct node-to-node tests
- Terraform: a stripped test module (tf-mod-priv-upgrades) used to inject a new load-balancer rule and a control-plane flag via a remote state override

Key experiments and findings:
1) TLS renegotiation with missing ALPN entries:
- Description: cp-lab-v2 advertises a new ALPN token (redwood-v2) in addition to tls/1.2. Old runtimes ignore unknown ALPN but some sidecar versions mis-handle extra ALPNs and close connections after accepting the TLS session.
- Symptom: gradual increase in connection churn, elevated p50 connection time, bursty 503s under sustained load.
- Mitigation: ensure cp advertises legacy-alpn first; add a temporary envoy filter to drop unknown ALPNs at ingress.
- Backout: revert envoy filter change and re-advertise legacy-only ALPN (control-plane flag).

2) Unary-to-streaming downgrade fallbacks:
- Description: New control-plane may open streaming sessions for event delivery; older runtimes fall back to unary but the load-balancer healthchecks wrongly assume stream semantics and mark nodes unhealthy.
- Symptom: nodes repeatedly cycled out of pool without obvious application errors, causing capacity loss during canary ramps.
- Mitigation: healthcheck shim that accepts both wire patterns; deploy as a short-lived proxy that translates streaming start frames to unary probes.
- Backout: remove shim and temporarily pin control-plane to unary-only feature gate.

3) Header size and compression mismatches:
- Description: cp-v2 increases metadata sizes (more trace headers). Older sidecar buffer thresholds caused aborted requests.
- Symptom: tail latency increases and TLS re-handshakes for large requests.
- Mitigation: increase sidecar/ingress header buffer limits in config; enable optional header compression on cp side for older clients.
- Backout: restore original buffer limits and disable compression flag.

Test matrix (what we ran) - short form:
- 0% canary, 5%, 20%, 50% traffic splits via weight-based routing
- Workloads: small prompt gen (short seq), long streaming chat (1k+ tokens), embedding requests (batch sizes 8–32)
- Observed metrics: conn_count, conn_churn_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate by code, LB healthy_count, TLS renegotiation_count

Gating thresholds (fail fast):
- error-rate (4xx/5xx combined) > 1.5x baseline for 10 minutes
- p95 latency > 2x baseline sustained for 5 minutes
- conn_churn_rate > baseline + 30% for 3 minutes
- healthy_count drop > 20% in pool size
If any trigger fires -> immediate step-down to previous control-plane image and revert any temporary envoy/stateful shims introduced in the session.

Terraform module notes (tf-mod-priv-upgrades):
- Keep changes small and idempotent: prefer a new bool feature flag resource for control-plane image flag rather than modify existing instance user-data templates.
- Use remote state override pattern for lab runs (module var: experiment_override = true) so changes can be destroyed quickly.
- When changing LB rules, apply with -target to LB resource only for canary injection then promote with a second apply for scaled shift.
- Avoid TF-driven DNS TTL changes during canary that cause clients to re-resolve during short windows (causes unexpected east-west connection patterns).

Compact deploy checklist (pre-canary):
- Confirm baseline telemetry (last 24h) uploaded and pinned in the console
- Create experiment remote state snapshot and tag in Git
- Deploy control-plane canary (single AZ, single LB node) with legacy feature flags on
- Apply envoy ingress filter that removes unknown ALPNs (lab only)
- Run smoke tests: simple generate, embed, and streaming connect (5 iterations each)
- Start synthetic load at 5% and watch gating thresholds for 10 minutes

Canary ramp plan (quick path):
- 0 -> 5% (10m) -> 20% (20m) -> 50% (20m) -> 100% (roll to all)
- At each step run the "light soak" suite (10m) then the "stress" suite (15m).
- For each step capture heap, conn table, and KV cache hit ratio snapshots.

Backout (fast) recipe - network/control-plane focused:
1) Pause routing change: set weight 0 for canary via LB control-plane API or rollback the tf LB change (use tf apply -target=module.lb to revert immediate routing).
2) Revert control-plane image via feature flag toggle (control-plane supports runtime feature flags published via etcd/kv) to previous stable image tag.
3) Remove any temporary ingress filters / envoy shims added for the session.
4) If LB healthy_count still low: trigger a graceful node recycle for effected runtimes (drain -> wait for connections to close -> uncordon).
5) If TLS handshake errors persist after revert: rotate certificates back to previous CA in the keychain and restart control-plane process (order: cp -> ingress -> runtime).
6) If problems persist beyond 30 minutes: escalate to SRE lead and follow full runtime rollback playbook.

Post-backout actions:
- Annotate the canary experiment with a brief failure summary and attach logs (cp and envoy)
- Capture pcap of a failed handshake and save to the lab bucket for analysis
- Create a follow-up ticket to harden the failing surface (example: sidecar upgrade path, add explicit ALPN negotiation tests in CI)

Observability and logging checklist (must-have for a successful rapid backout):
- Control-plane debug logs at TRACE for negotiation paths (auto-enable for canary)
- Envoy stats exported to Prometheus with per-route ALPN and reject counters
- LB and host-level kernel TCP metrics (retransmits, RSTs) captured by node exporter
- Short retention pcap capture for 30 minutes around the canary window

Known limitations and open questions:
- Some on-prem firewalls drop TCP connections with unusual ALPN lists — need a discovery playbook for customer firewalls before production push.
- KV migration: experiments didn't cover very large KV sync windows (>50GB). Plan a separate staged state migration with throttled sync.
- HSM-backed key rotations during a canary are high-risk — recommend separate maintenance window.

Appendix: quick commands (lab)
- Revert LB weight via terraform (targeted): terraform apply -target=module.lb -var='weight=0' -auto-approve
- Toggle control-plane gate via etcd key: curl -XPOST ${CP_ADMIN}/feature-toggle -d '{"legacy-alpn": true}'
- Enable sidecar verbose logs: kubectl -n ingress set env ds/envoy LOG_LEVEL=debug

Next steps:
- Add an explicit CI test that opens TLS sessions advertising extra ALPN tokens and validates no sidecar connection churn
- Draft a short customer-facing guidance doc on firewall compatibility for ALPN/large-header scenarios
- Schedule a follow-up lab to exercise KV migration patterns with incremental sync sizes

Notes to reviewer:
This doc aims to be pragmatic and compact for on-call and lab engineers who need a fast backout path that does not require full runtime binary rollbacks. It's intentionally focused on connection-level failure modes which historically are small changes that cause outsized disruptions in private deployments. Please add lab observability links and any missing run commands you used locally.
